tasks.title: Scan the pitch and find the way in

does.text: A prospect reads each network's partner pages, then writes to a regional mailbox, fills a contact form or books an account executive to start talks.

touchpoints.name: American Express Global Network contact form

why.text: Every route ends in a form, a mailbox or an account executive, and only Visa publishes licensing steps before contact.

points.text: Visa's community contact route opens a newsletter sign-up, so intent is captured as a marketing lead.
The Amex network form offers no community bank, credit union or fintech business type.
Discover's partnering page promises consultation and co-creation, then ends at a contact form with nine US categories.
Evaluation pages go stale, with Visa's Fast Track citing a 2022 fact sheet and Amex's issuer page a 2022 ranking.

discover.text: Discover sends every partner type to a contact form, while PULSE promises a sales callback within two business days.

opportunity.title: One front door that names the next step
opportunity.text: One intake routes each prospect by partner type and states the next step, who owns it and the committed reply time. The prospect no longer guesses which form or mailbox fits.
opportunity.stage_move: One front door that names the next step

tasks.title: Shortlist a platform that carries the network

does.text: A fintech looks for a BIN sponsor, issuer processor or programme manager that can issue on each network, often through network enabler directories.

why.text: Visa and Mastercard directories help a fintech shortlist enablers, while four of six issuing platforms checked document no Discover issuing.

points.text: Stripe, Adyen, Lithic and Highnote document no Discover issuing, and SoFi Tech Solutions says the primary network is usually Visa or Mastercard.
A fintech guide drops Discover and Amex as three-party networks and says incumbent incentives are hard for startups to win.
Visa's directory listed 73 partners in September 2026, while its pages speak of hundreds.
Mastercard tells users to run their own due diligence on the partners it lists.

discover.text: Discover's fintech page names no processor, sponsor bank or programme manager, although Marqeta says it is certified on Discover's 2026 release.

opportunity.title: A provider shelf for fintechs
opportunity.text: Publish the processors, sponsor banks and programme managers that carry the network, by product and country. The fintech then starts its path inside a platform it can already use.
opportunity.stage_move: A provider shelf for fintechs

tasks.title: Read the specifications and try a sandbox

does.text: A developer reads the API documentation, gets sandbox keys and calls test endpoints to judge the build before any commercial talk.

why.text: Visa and Mastercard open documentation and sandboxes, while Amex reviews key requests and Discover admits developers only by invitation.

points.text: Discover's Developer Center admits developers by representative invitation after a contact form.
Discover's catalogue is partial, pricing is absent and no llms.txt is published.
Five of 18 Amex products hold specifications for invited readers, and Amex reviews each sandbox key request.
No API prices are published, and Visa's pricing page explains three fee models without amounts.

discover.text: Twelve Partner Product Portal products show OpenAPI specifications signed out, yet a key still needs a representative.

opportunity.title: Open evaluation for developers
opportunity.text: Specifications, sandbox keys and a pricing model page open before any representative contact, with markdown twins for coding assistants. The developer can judge the build alone.
opportunity.stage_move: Open evaluation for developers

tasks.title: Model the yield and weigh incumbent incentives

does.text: An issuer models interchange yield against incumbent incentives, often through paid advisers or pooled buyers who run bids between Visa and Mastercard.

why.text: The harm evidence rests on DOJ allegations of cliff pricing at Visa and on participant submissions to the RBA, so issuers face real uncertainty without shown repeated loss.

points.text: One adviser says many community institutions sign without benchmark data.
The Fed says its interchange table does not show what an issuer would earn on a network.
Analysts expect Visa to claw back discounts across a defecting bank's portfolio, which is opinion.
Visa's benchmark tool opens only after an issuer joins its programme through Visa Online.

discover.text: PULSE offers a scheduled Debit Advantage Analysis and switcher case studies, though the all-in fee and exempt rates stay unpublished.

opportunity.title: A self-serve debit yield model
opportunity.text: Turn the Debit Advantage Analysis into a model a prospect runs on its own mix, with assumptions visible. The issuer sees exempt yield after routing before any call.
opportunity.stage_move: A self-serve debit yield model

tasks.title: See the acceptance price before signing

does.text: An acquirer, ISO or ATM operator looks for interchange, network fees and connection costs to price a new acceptance line.

touchpoints.name: Visa U.S.A. Interchange Reimbursement Fees PDF
Mastercard Connect Pricing and Billing Center

why.text: Regulators stepped in on fee visibility, with the PSR finding poor fee information imposed costs and Canada and the RBA requiring networks to publish their fees.

points.text: Visa publishes interchange as a dated PDF, while its network fee schedules stay unpublished.
Mastercard bills registration fees whose amounts sit in the gated Pricing and Billing Center.
A prospective acquirer cannot see Discover's US economics before signing up and being issued a code.
PULSE's ATM page states competitive fees without figures and closes on a contact route.

discover.text: Discover's US acquirer schedule sits behind an acquirer-issued code, while its Canadian schedule is public.

opportunity.title: Price visible to a stranger
opportunity.text: An acquirer or ATM operator sees a standard schedule and fee structure before sign-up, as Discover already shows in Canada. Incentives sit on a separate line.
opportunity.stage_move: Price visible to a stranger

tasks.title: Run due diligence on the network and its owner

does.text: An issuer's team checks the network's standing, endorsements and ownership, often with a trade body report or a paid adviser.

why.text: Issuers weigh an owner that competes with banks for deposits, and much of the proof on offer is dated or self-reported.

points.text: Discover's owner competes with banks for deposits, and neither merger approval set a condition on network access.
Capital One warns it may be unable to offer adequate pricing to network partners.
A Datos analyst expected banks that see Capital One as a competitor to drop PULSE, which is opinion.
PULSE's reconciliation and switching claims are its own and are not independently checked.

discover.text: ABA endorses Discover Debit and offers a due diligence report, a structured evaluation artefact no rival shows publicly.

opportunity.title: An evaluation pack per partner type
opportunity.text: Each prospect downloads a pack with the participation model, fee structure lines, committed service levels, ownership separation terms and endorsements. The study infers the network then sets the terms of comparison.
opportunity.stage_move: An evaluation pack per partner type

tasks.title: Make the merchant case for carrying the brand

does.text: Acquirers, ISOs and ATM processors decide whether to sell a network's acceptance, and merchants ask what volume it brings.

why.text: Merchants ask what volume a network brings, and Discover's public pages give reach counts without a spend figure.

points.text: No seller kit or objection guide for Discover acceptance was found on the public sites.
Independent ATM operators buy processing that bundles the PIN debit networks, so the processor makes the network choice.
Discover's US acquirer list omits Adyen, Chase and Worldpay.
OptBlue sellers work under non-public Operating Regulations held by the Participant.

discover.text: ISOs and payfacs can register on EASI for technical material, yet get no sales kit.

opportunity.title: Arm the channel that sells
opportunity.text: Acquirers, ISOs and ATM processors get a seller kit with merchant-level value evidence, dated peer proof and objection answers. The network's case then reaches merchants through the channel.
opportunity.stage_move: Arm the channel that sells

tasks.title: Choose the join route and secure a sponsor

does.text: Most partners join through a sponsor bank or principal, which registers them, carries their liability and sets its own terms.

touchpoints.name: Visa Licensing Program page, Associate tier

why.text: Sponsors keep wide discretion over terms, and a route can close, as Mastercard's Type I processor route did in May 2025.

points.text: Only banks, or processors a bank approves, may send ATM transactions, so losing a sponsor can halt operations.
Network standards stop a sponsored acquirer settling funds itself, which binds it to the sponsor bank.
A Mastercard principal needs approval to sponsor a programme manager, and that approval is revocable without notice.
A former ISO owner says vertical software firms do not know how to structure a sponsor bank relationship.

discover.text: Discover tells payment facilitators to find an acquiring bank in each market, and PULSE publishes no membership types or sponsor model.

opportunity.title: One join map per partner type
opportunity.text: Each partner type gets a path stating who signs, whether a sponsor is needed, the documents asked for and the identifiers issued. A payfac or credit union sees its route before any call.
opportunity.stage_move: One join map per partner type

tasks.title: Apply for a direct licence and pass the review

does.text: A bank confirms eligibility, completes the application and answers the network's review of regulatory permissions, AML, credit and settlement risk.

touchpoints.name: Visa Access Client Lifecycle Management Tool
Discover Partner Product Portal, Going Live

why.text: Applicants cannot self-assess eligibility or timing, since eligibility rules sit outside the public rulebook and no licensing timeline was found.

points.text: Visa's eligibility rules live in charter documents outside the public rulebook.
The study found no licensing timeline from any of the four networks.
Mastercard may demand capital, collateral or escrow, and Amex asks for an investment-grade rating or a guarantee.
Amex hands over its rulebooks only after the agreement is signed.

discover.text: Discover routes issuers to a contact form or a Diners mailbox, and its five-stage Going Live flow is not a readable page.

opportunity.title: Service levels on the network's own steps
opportunity.text: State the network's response time for credentials, registration review and reconsideration of a refusal, and show it on each step. The applicant can plan against a date.
opportunity.stage_move: Service levels on the network's own steps

tasks.title: Register as a technology provider

does.text: A processor, gateway or software vendor registers its company, accepts terms and gets its first user into the network's provider portal.

why.text: Visa says developer onboarding can take two weeks or several months, and Discover splits access across two doors.

points.text: Visa Developer credentials beyond sandbox need a signed contract, collected in an Onboarding Dashboard.
Discover's Developer Center is invite-only, while EASI is self-service.
The EASI Registration Guide PDF returned a server error on 26 September 2026.
Mastercard routes a company it cannot link to a Connect profile into due diligence with a reference number.

discover.text: EASI offers self-registration across eighteen company types, while API access still needs an invitation.

opportunity.title: Carry one application record forward
opportunity.text: Later onboarding tasks pre-fill from what the partner gave at registration, so EASI data flows into the Going Live stages. The partner enters its company once.
opportunity.stage_move: Carry one application record forward

tasks.title: Sign the agreement and brand licence

does.text: The partner signs a participation agreement and a marks licence, with fees negotiated inside the contract.

touchpoints.name: Mastercard Connect Pricing and Billing Center

why.text: Most joining fees are unpublished, and Amex obligations cannot be read before signing.

points.text: Visa's last public agent fee dates from 2016, and Mastercard's registration fees sit behind Connect.
PULSE agreements usually auto-renew and add participation and membership fees whose amounts are not published.
OptBlue forbids Participants to publish the wholesale fee, yet processor guides listing every tier sit openly on bank and reseller sites.
Amex issuers pay a monthly rental fee for each active BIN, USD 175 in the 2023 manual.

discover.text: Like its rivals, the Discover family keeps fees inside agreements, with PULSE fees named in filings without amounts and Diners interchange negotiated per issuer.

opportunity.title: Say plainly what joining costs
opportunity.text: Publish registration and participation fees on the join map, or state that a step carries no fee. The partner can budget before it signs.
opportunity.stage_move: Say plainly what joining costs

tasks.title: Register agents and third parties

does.text: The sponsor vets each ISO, payment facilitator or ATM deployer, then registers it with each network before any service starts.

touchpoints.name: Visa Global Registry of Service Providers
Amex Payment Facilitator Registration Form, Appendix G

why.text: Registration runs on per-acquirer cases, emailed PDFs and sponsor spreadsheets, with assessments for missed steps.

points.text: An agent serving several acquirers is registered separately by each.
Amex registration runs on PDFs and a shared mailbox, and no status view is published.
Missing a Mastercard registration step can cost the sponsor up to USD 25,000 for each 30 days.
Sponsor job postings describe the work as case work tracked in Excel.

discover.text: Discover publishes no network-level registration step, form or fee for ISOs or payment facilitators, and no registration status to check.

opportunity.title: A sponsor console for third-party registration
opportunity.text: The sponsor keeps one record per ISO, payment facilitator or ATM deployer, holding the diligence checklist, PCI evidence and identifiers. Status stays visible up to written approval.
opportunity.stage_move: A sponsor console for third-party registration

tasks.title: Receive identifiers and name the contacts

does.text: At approval the partner receives its BIN, ICA or participant numbers, then enters named contacts in each network's directory.

why.text: Identifiers and contacts arrive through several tools, each with its own deadline.

points.text: Visa members must enter named contacts in the Client Directory within 10 business days of a BIN going live.
Mastercard ties each ICA and BIN to a country, and adding a country means a new application.
When a portfolio changes hands, the new owner has 10 calendar days to file or Visa may delete the BINs.
Several Visa pages still name Visa Online after its rename to Visa Access, leaving two names for one portal.

discover.text: EASI captures a signing authority at registration, and Going Live names an Organization Identification stage with no public detail.

opportunity.title: Named roles captured once at joining
opportunity.text: Collect the signing authority, senior officer, operations lead and portal administrator in the first form. The network reuses them for access, bulletins and escalation.
opportunity.stage_move: Named roles captured once at joining

tasks.title: Get portal access and set up administrators

does.text: The partner registers for each network portal, names its administrators and provisions staff to each application and data scope.

why.text: Set-up runs on emailed forms, hand-passed passwords and separate entry routes, each with its own turnaround.

points.text: Mastercard's form 1145 names Security Administrators by email, and their RSA tokens arrive by encrypted email.
Visa Enrollment Manager shows a temporary password that the administrator passes to the new user by hand.
A small bank inherits the same two-administrator model and form process as a large one.
A company already on EASI cannot register again, and the user must email to join the existing profile.

discover.text: EASI, PULSE and the Service Center fraud products each have their own entry route, though EASI review usually takes two business days.

opportunity.title: One door for the Discover family
opportunity.text: EASI, PULSE, the Developer Center and fraud product enrolment sit behind one registration and one record. The partner signs in once and sees every tool it holds.
opportunity.stage_move: One door for the Discover family

tasks.title: Configure the programme and enrol in services

does.text: The issuer gives the network its processing parameters and enrols in optional services, often through forms and guides from its representative.

touchpoints.name: Visa Program Request Management, eCIQ and VCSA
Mastercard Customer Operations Services participation form

why.text: Key guides and forms come through representatives, and a programme manager may own a token project that spans networks, wallets and processor.

points.text: Visa's regional implementation guides for optional services come from the Visa representative.
Visa Token Service onboarding material is restricted to entitled users, so the issuer path is not public.
For MDES Token Connect the issuer first sends wireframes for Mastercard to review against a design checklist.
Thredd tells a programme manager it owns the token project and must manage the networks, wallets and processor itself.

discover.text: Discover's issuer certification steps are not public, and the D-PAS Certification Manual is referenced without being published.

opportunity.title: One certification record with an owner on every step
opportunity.text: One project record, read by partner and network staff, shows each step's owner, state and sign-off. The partner sees who holds the next move.
opportunity.stage_move: One certification record with an owner on every step

tasks.title: Certify the host with the network

does.text: The acquirer, issuer processor or direct merchant runs authorisation and clearing tests against a network simulator, usually scheduled or reviewed by network staff, and receives a completion letter.

why.text: Host certification is representative-led at every network, and the reported losses of weeks and CEDP rates each come from a single vendor, so the level is notable.

points.text: Visa's host path waits on a representative to schedule attended testing through VCMS.
Discover's certification forms and test keys come from an implementation manager, and keys can arrive by encrypted email.
Mastercard acquirers send simulator logs to an implementation specialist for review.
An acquirer not activated for a response code receives a generic decline, so activation gaps look like issuer declines.

discover.text: Discover's designated simulator shows results as partners test with no logs to submit, and Discover reviews results within agreed service levels.

opportunity.title: Live simulator results with a committed review
opportunity.text: Partners self-test at any time, see each case pass or fail and hand the batch to review under a stated service level. The request form's colour checks run as the partner types.
opportunity.stage_move: Live simulator results with a committed review

tasks.title: Certify terminals and file for the letter

does.text: The acquirer describes each terminal configuration, runs L3 or end-to-end tests, often through an accredited provider, and files results for a letter.

touchpoints.name: Discover Terminal E2E Certification Request Form
D-PAS Terminal E2E Letter of Certification

why.text: Combinations of devices, software and acquirers multiply the certifications, and scheduling and reviews drive the calendar time.

points.text: Each network closes with a different artefact, and Visa issues no letter for L3, so the CCRT email is the only proof.
Discover's forms and qualified tool list come only from the implementation manager.
Discover waivers expire and cover only terminal certification, so an open host fix is tracked outside the letter.
Amex's published certification steps all start with the relationship manager.

discover.text: Discover matches peers on self-certification and per-acquirer test cases, and gives up to ten full sets of test cards free.

opportunity.title: A wallet of certification letters
opportunity.text: Every letter sits in the record with its tested configuration, waivers and expiry dates. The partner shares proof with a client or reuses it on a new implementation.
opportunity.stage_move: A wallet of certification letters

tasks.title: Certify once for many clients

does.text: A processor, gateway or programme manager certifies its platform so clients inherit the result, then gets registered by each acquirer or bank it serves. It recertifies each network release and tells clients whether to act.

touchpoints.name: Mastercard Developers 'on behalf of a client' project flag
Processor mandate logs such as Marqeta's and SoFi's

why.text: Mastercard supports reuse, while Visa registers agents per acquirer and Tap to Phone certification can take a year.

points.text: Each acquirer registers an agent separately, so a processor serving many acquirers is registered many times.
Visa Ready Tap to Phone certification typically takes six to twelve months, and lab testing can cost 50,000 dollars or more.
Several leading issuing platforms have not built for Discover, so their fintech clients cannot reach it.
Discover accredits acquirers for AMTC case by case, and its type approval process is not described publicly.

discover.text: Discover accredits processors indirectly and case by case, though processors report few Discover mandate changes.

opportunity.title: Build for the processor as the customer
opportunity.text: Let a processor act for many clients in one place, passing on its certification and showing which clients inherit it. Each client sees its own record read-only.
opportunity.stage_move: Certify once, inherit across clients

tasks.title: Certify ATMs and keep locations current

does.text: An ATM acquirer or its ISO runs L3 testing on its machines, certifies added services and updates location records every quarter.

why.text: ATM work stacks L3 testing, service certification and quarterly location updates across a sponsor and ISO chain.

points.text: A test-tool vendor estimates ATM end-to-end PCI certification effort at 40 to 50 percent, overlapping Windows 10 migration.
Adding cash advance or balance inquiry to an ATM needs specific network testing, including host testing.
Mastercard requires quarterly ATM location updates in a separate Connect tool.
Cirrus forwards ATM balance inquiries only to issuers certified for them by Customer Operations Services.

discover.text: PULSE gives ATM acquirers a list tool and gateway access, and no public source describes PULSE or Discover ATM certification.

opportunity.title: The ATM chain in one view
opportunity.text: Show the sponsor bank, ISO, processor and each network registration for an operator's fleet. Location upkeep sits in the same record.
opportunity.stage_move: The ATM chain in one view

tasks.title: Check whether a change needs retesting

does.text: Before changing a kernel, gateway, device or message format, the partner works out whether the change needs network testing or only internal regression.

touchpoints.name: Discover Terminal E2E Certification Request Form

why.text: Retest triggers when anything in the chain changes are a named friction, and the agreed rules sit in a forum FAQ with no interactive check.

points.text: When an ISO buys a portfolio and routes devices through a new gateway, the terminals must be retested.
Visa's 2016 guide requires a retest if production starts more than 90 days after testing.
A move to a new message format is a major change that needs the networks involved.
Under Discover's 2011 rules a direct merchant certified every new data link, processor switch and large system rewrite.

discover.text: Discover's request form lists the events that trigger terminal recertification, which matches the networks' jointly agreed retest rules.

opportunity.title: A retest check before any change
opportunity.text: The partner describes a change and sees whether it is minor, needs internal regression or needs network testing. Discover's listed triggers give the check a ready rule set.
opportunity.stage_move: A retest check before any change

tasks.title: Open a developer account and get sandbox keys

does.text: A developer registers on the network's portal, creates a project, picks APIs and receives sandbox credentials for a first call. At Visa and Mastercard this happens the same day without a representative.

touchpoints.name: Mastercard Developers Create new project screen
Discover Developer Center Contact Us form

why.text: Discover and American Express put a person between sign-up and a first call, and some Mastercard sandboxes wait for a service team.

points.text: Discover admits developers only when a representative sends an invitation, and its own guide says both self-register and invitation only.
American Express keeps each product in Requested until it approves, and no product offers instant sandbox access.
Some Mastercard sandboxes sit Under Review, and a forum post shows a correctly signed call failing at SANDBOX Pending.
Mastercard has no portal-wide set of test cards, and Visa's SDKs and sample code sit behind sign-in.

discover.text: Discover publishes twelve readable OpenAPI specifications, yet no developer can reach its sandbox without a representative's invitation.

opportunity.title: Sandbox key on the first visit
opportunity.text: A signed-up developer would create a project, get sandbox credentials and published test cards, and call the twelve existing APIs with no representative. This matches Visa and Mastercard and passes the American Express key review.
opportunity.stage_move: A sandbox key on the first visit

tasks.title: Obtain the host interface specifications

does.text: An acquirer or issuer processor fetches the confidential ISO 8583 host specifications from the network's gated site and builds authorisation and clearing to them. Networks reissue them with release-named changes.

touchpoints.name: Mastercard Technical Resource Center on Mastercard Connect

why.text: All four networks keep the specifications as confidential manuals behind a login, and Mastercard readers track changes by PDF search.

points.text: Mastercard Connect needs an account set up through a representative and an RSA SecurID token to sign in.
Readers find Mastercard specification changes by searching the PDF for *chg* markers.
Hosts must process new DE 48 subelements that Mastercard has not announced.
EASI rejects personal email addresses, and Discover's fuller IIN table needs an NDA on file.

discover.text: Discover gates its specifications in EASI like its rivals, and EASI self-registers with a stated two-day review.

opportunity.title: Specifications as versioned, diffable pages
opportunity.text: Entitled users would read the host specification as searchable pages with a per-release change list, and anyone could read a public field map for feasibility. All four networks ship manuals today, while Mastercard shows a public mapping works.
opportunity.stage_move: Specifications by entitlement, versioned and diffable

tasks.title: Set up and renew keys and certificates

does.text: The developer generates keys and certificates for each environment, builds keystores and adds layers such as mutual TLS and JWE encryption. It renews them before they expire.

touchpoints.name: Amex Project Dashboard To Do items

why.text: The friction falls at occasional moments, a lost one-time key or an expiry, which cost a new project or a request.

points.text: Visa's private key downloads only once, so a lost key means a new project.
Discover's Consumer Application Certificate downloads only once, and a replacement needs a request.
Mastercard keys expire after 13 months, and two of its documents disagree on the reminder schedule.
Visa sends certificate expiry emails only for certification and production projects.

discover.text: Discover matches Visa's one-time certificate download, while Mastercard now automates production mutual TLS certificates.

opportunity.title: Self-service key reissue with reminders
opportunity.text: Developers would re-download or reissue their own keys and certificates, with renewal reminders in every environment. Mastercard already automates production certificates, so this closes a gap.
opportunity.stage_move: Credentials that do not strand the developer

tasks.title: Enable token services and wallet provisioning

does.text: An issuer connects to the network's token service for wallets and stored credentials, and a merchant or PSP registers as a token requestor with notification endpoints. Most steps run through a network or processor contact.

touchpoints.name: Visa Acceptance Token Management Service guide
Discover Stored Token Services API Specs tab

why.text: Token services are the least self-serve build surface, with an account executive, delivery manager or representative in the path at each network.

points.text: Mastercard's issuer token API has no sandbox, and test evidence travels as an Excel file by email.
Visa Acceptance asks partners to email merchant details to support in the middle of an API-driven flow.
A community bank told the FDIC its debit tokenisation stalled while it waited on its core provider.
The Amex sandbox does not save token state, so lifecycle tests always return Active.

discover.text: Discover's token API is fully specified in public, yet it sits in the invitation-only Developer Center with no published webhook retry or signing detail.

opportunity.title: Token requestor onboarding without email
opportunity.text: A merchant or wallet would get a token requestor ID and register notification endpoints in the portal, with PULSE Side-by-Side offered in the same flow. Visa Acceptance, Amex and Mastercard each insert an email or representative step.
opportunity.stage_move: Token requestor onboarding without email

tasks.title: Request production access and credentials

does.text: The developer submits company, ownership and use-case details, waits for review and a contract, then generates production credentials. Discover repeats its registration for production and issues a new credential set.

touchpoints.name: Visa Going live form and Onboarding Dashboard

why.text: Timing is uncertain, with Visa stating no review timeline and quoting two weeks to several months for onboarding.

points.text: Visa says timing is the first question on nearly every client's mind.
The Amex Move to Production link reopens the To Do list for a second review.
Visa certification and production credentials need a new CSR per environment and appear only after signature.
Discover repeats the registration process for production and issues new credentials.

discover.text: Discover repeats its representative-led process for production, while Mastercard verifies a company instantly when it is linked to Mastercard Connect.

opportunity.title: Committed times on the network's own steps
opportunity.text: Each Discover step, such as registration or production review, would show its committed time and an escalation route. Discover already states a two-day EASI review and PULSE five days, and Mastercard pairs service levels with escalation.
opportunity.stage_move: State the network's own service levels

tasks.title: Get card designs and wallet art approved

does.text: The issuer, often through its card manufacturer, submits each card design for network approval and loads separate art for wallets and token requestors. Fintech programmes add the sponsor bank's approval of all card art.

touchpoints.name: Mastercard Card Design Standards on Mastercard Connect

why.text: Visa and Mastercard gate design approval and its standards behind a login, and platforms quote weeks for approval plus months of production.

points.text: Platform guides quote 1 to 3 weeks for design approval and 8 to 10 weeks of card production.
A new tokenised card image can take up to 10 days to reach cardholders' wallets.
Processors load wallet art separately in Visa's VCMM and the Mastercard portal, keyed to the manufacturer's reference.
Visa says its design approval gives no legal protection, so issuers still run their own legal review.

discover.text: No public document shows how Discover approves Discover or Diners Club card designs, though Discover Debit issuers get card art through the Marketing Hub.

opportunity.title: Card art once, used everywhere
opportunity.text: One card art submission would drive design approval, wallet and token art and Marketing Hub collateral. The issuer, processor and card vendor would all see its status.
opportunity.stage_move: Card art once, used everywhere

tasks.title: Register the programme and clear launch marketing

does.text: Before launch the partner registers the programme, or its riskier merchants, with the network. It then submits campaigns, co-brand partners and press releases for review.

touchpoints.name: Visa Program Information Form on Visa Partner

why.text: Each network adds its own pre-launch approvals, with co-brand submissions due at American Express 60 business days ahead.

points.text: Co-brand partners go to American Express at least 60 business days before launch.
A launch press release naming the network needs the network's pre-approval.
Mastercard warned new issuers that billing and settlement start once the ICA is assigned, before any card is live.
Registering a Mastercard service provider took about 5 to 7 business days in 2011.

discover.text: Discover publishes no application steps, timelines or fees for new issuing partners, and its fintech route names no launch steps.

opportunity.title: Committed review times on each launch task
opportunity.text: Where Discover commits to a review time, for card art, marketing or co-brand review, the task would show it and leave estimates out. American Express already writes such windows into its policies.
opportunity.stage_move: Show committed review service levels

tasks.title: Load new card ranges into routing tables

does.text: The acquirer or ATM acquirer receives each network's range table and installs it within the deadline, so new cards route correctly and avoid declines.

touchpoints.name: Discover BIN file and EASI range table

why.text: Deadlines run from 3 to 6 days, and Mastercard puts the fix for stale-table declines on the acquirer.

points.text: Visa gives 6 business days and Mastercard 6 calendar days to install each update.
Stale tables cause wrong routing and declines.
Discover's public BIN file shows only start, end and length, and the full table sits in EASI under NDA.
Accepting alliance cards and Discover Debit depends on the acquirer loading every Discover range.

discover.text: Discover's full range table needs an NDA, and its public file lacks product detail.

opportunity.title: Range readiness before cards ship
opportunity.text: Discover would publish new ranges with effective dates and show issuers which major acquirers have loaded them before cards go out. No public source shows a network telling issuers whether acceptance is ready.
opportunity.stage_move: Range readiness before cards ship

tasks.title: Run a pilot and get the go-ahead to launch

does.text: The partner finishes certification, runs any pilot or beta test and waits for confirmation that it may go live. American Express is the only network whose public rules define this gate for issuers.

touchpoints.name: Amex Beta Test and go-ahead notice
Visa Client Directory on Visa Access
Going Live with Discover phase table

why.text: Visa and Mastercard define no pilot and no single live moment, so partners piece together their own proof of launch.

points.text: Visa's rules name no notice that a programme is live, so the issuer's own directory update is the nearest confirmation.
Mastercard Send asks partners to confirm go-live by finding their transactions in reconciliation reports.
Every American Express design change reopens a Beta Test of up to 60 days.
American Express charges 15,000 dollars for each issuer personalisation certification it leads.

discover.text: Discover's Letter of Certification records scope, versions and waivers, and its API go-live ends in a launch step with Discover support and monitoring.

opportunity.title: A written go-ahead that says you are live
opportunity.text: Go-live would become one network-issued notice listing what was certified, the sample card or test result approved, the effective date and the first live transactions seen. It would extend the Letter of Certification partners already know.
opportunity.stage_move: A written go-ahead that says you are live

tasks.title: Put up acceptance marks and signage

does.text: Merchants and ATM acquirers display network marks within set deadlines, and issuers bring cards into line with mark rules. Acquirers and sales agents order signage for the merchants they sign.

why.text: Deadlines are published and signage is free, so the effort lies in separate ordering sites and rules that are partly private.

points.text: Discover's signage ordering site needs a separate login or registration.
The PULSE Operating Rules are not public, so only excerpts quoted in the graphic manual can be read.
Under Discover's 2011 rules, improper mark use cost 2,500 dollars per violation after any cure period.
Mastercard debit issuers have nine months to issue compliant cards and 36 months to bring the portfolio into line.

discover.text: PULSE publishes its mark files and deadlines openly, while Discover merchants and agents order signage on a separate gated site with no agent hub.

opportunity.title: Marks and deadlines inside the launch checklist
opportunity.text: Mark rules, downloads, signage ordering and post-launch deadlines would sit in the partner's launch checklist, with bulk ordering for acquirers and agents. American Express already gives agents bulk signage ordering.
opportunity.stage_move: Marks and deadlines inside the launch checklist

tasks.title: Watch the first weeks of live traffic

does.text: After go-live the partner checks its first transactions, approvals and early disputes and reports progress to the network, at times with a named implementation lead.

why.text: Partners carry early monitoring themselves, with payfacs watching every sponsored merchant, Amex issuers filing monthly progress reports and Visa charging per-item VAMP fees since October 2025.

points.text: The Mastercard Send Delivery Manager monitors the project, so escalation depends on one person.
Amex issuers file monthly Program Progress Reports within 15 days of month-end from launch.
Payfacs must monitor every sponsored merchant, and Visa's per-item VAMP fees began in October 2025.
Visa's acquirer monitoring flags whole portfolios at 50 and 70 basis points of fraud and disputes.

discover.text: Discover already promises launch support and monitoring and names an implementation project manager for Discover Debit issuers.

opportunity.title: A shared first-weeks launch room
opportunity.text: A launch view would show approval rates, declines by reason, disputes and the named implementation lead, then hand over to account management. Visa's prescriptive new-merchant checks are ending, which leaves the gap open.
opportunity.stage_move: A shared first-weeks launch room

tasks.title: Reissue a converted portfolio in waves

does.text: An issuer moving networks reissues cards in pilot groups and waves, runs an overlap window and pushes new details through account updaters. Members may need new PINs and must update recurring payments.

why.text: Public conversions show cardholders and merchants repeatedly losing money and service, from 1.5 million calls at one cutover to uncapped debit rates.

points.text: Citi logged over 1.5 million service calls when Costco's cards moved on a single day.
Capital One cardholders lost Mastercard benefits on activation, and some payroll and earned-wage providers dropped instant transfers.
Reissuing a whole BIN range at once breaks stored credentials, and account updaters reach participating merchants only.
Travellers were told to plan for acceptance abroad, and merchants met uncapped debit rates they cannot avoid.

discover.text: Discover offers other issuers no public conversion kit, while Visa's updater carries portfolios into Visa and, outside Latin America, none out.

opportunity.title: A conversion kit built from the Capital One reissue
opportunity.text: Conversion would come as a tracked plan covering pilot waves, the overlap window, updater coverage, merchant and payroll notices and acceptance where cardholders travel. Discover is the only network that has just run a large public conversion.
opportunity.stage_move: A conversion kit built from the Capital One reissue

tasks.title: Collect the day's clearing and settlement files

does.text: Operations staff pull each network's daily settlement reports and clearing files, often forwarded by a processor. Visa sends VSS reports, Mastercard six GCMS cycles and Amex a Daily Activity Report.

touchpoints.name: GCMS cycle reports IP727010-AA, IP727020-AA, IP728010-AA
Mastercard File Express Client and Scheduler
Daily Activity Report and Daily Activity File
Discover daily clearing file and 14:00 fee file

why.text: Late network files are the main cause of settlement data delays at one processor, and a Mastercard sender without a confirmation file must phone to check.

points.text: Mastercard stopped phoning acquirers about risk rejects, and a sender with no confirmation file must phone to learn whether its file was processed.
Downgrade and reject reports missing from a daily package cannot be recreated later, and recreating expired Mastercard clearing data costs a per-file fee.
Programmes behind a processor cannot choose their own Visa reports. Marqeta tells customers to ask their Visa representative which VSS reports they can receive.
Processor guides disagree on the calendar. Paymentology says there is no Sunday clearing, while the 2021 GCMS manual schedules Sunday cycles.

discover.text: Discover runs one clearing cycle a day, with files arriving between 10:00 and 14:00 and network fees in a separate 14:00 file.

opportunity.title: Each settlement day shown as a status
opportunity.text: Show each settlement day and each file as pending or complete, with a notice when a network file is late. Stripe and Lithic already treat completeness as a state, while Mastercard makes senders phone to confirm a file.
opportunity.stage_move: Settlement day as a status

tasks.title: Reconcile the daily settlement to the funds moved

does.text: The partner ties clearing records and settlement reports, layer by layer, to the net amount wired that day. A payfac also funds and reconciles each sub-merchant daily.

why.text: Issuers rebuild Mastercard fund reconciliation from documentation fragments and spreadsheets, and Visa and Mastercard sell training on the task.

points.text: A disputed Mastercard advisement must be raised in writing within one business day and still paid in full, with daily assessments from USD 250 for missed settlement.
Clearing that arrives after the Visa cut-off is reported under a different settlement service heading, which a reconciler must know to match totals.
Mastercard expects its debit switch totals and processor totals to differ at times, and its reports omit transaction types with no activity.
A sponsor bank says funding reconciliation is more burdensome under the payfac model.

discover.text: PULSE Gateway settles many ATM and POS networks through one system on one cutoff, with exception items for all of them in PULSE PIX2.

opportunity.title: Totals guaranteed to tie to the wire
opportunity.text: State the settlement arithmetic on screen and show each day that report totals equal the funds moved. Amex, Mastercard Send and Discover's own old report show the tie-out can be promised.
opportunity.stage_move: Totals that tie to the wire

tasks.title: Balance ATM settlement terminal by terminal

does.text: Operators reconcile each terminal, matching withdrawals, surcharge and settlement dates to deposits and allowing for funds in transit. Vault cash and surcharge settle the next banking day, and interchange arrives monthly.

touchpoints.name: PULSE Debit Dashboard, PULSE ATM module

why.text: Operator statements stack several layers of fees, and a software vendor says many operators reconcile in separate systems with spreadsheets filling the gaps.

points.text: Network fees on surcharged withdrawals and EMV fallback fees reach operators only if their processor passes them through.
Cardtronics alleges Visa deducts its acquirer fee from issuer-paid interchange, and that Visa raised that fee from 6 to 16 cents in 2012.
A processor tells operators network penalties can reach $50,000 per event per device.

discover.text: PULSE settles gateway activity at a single point, yet publishes no ATM interchange amounts for operators to check their statements against.

opportunity.title: A per-terminal statement by network
opportunity.text: Give operators and their processors a per-terminal view of interchange by network, net of network fees, with each fee named. The study found no network offering operators this view directly.
opportunity.stage_move: An ATM statement by terminal and network

tasks.title: Check interchange qualification and chase downgrades

does.text: Acquirers and their processors pre-qualify each transaction, then find network downgrades after the fact in processor reports. Merchants ask their processor for downgrade reports.

touchpoints.name: DGN service centre acquirer interchange page

why.text: The Fed found acquirers and merchants paid commercial interchange on about five million Discover consumer cards from 2007 to at least 2023 without being told.

points.text: Mastercard's parameter file lists rate designators but omits the rates, so acquirers cannot compute expected interchange from it.
A failing Mastercard rate designator falls to the next one, and US consumer credit failures land at a Standard rate of 3.15% plus USD 0.10.
The interchange fee line on Visa SMS detail reports is off by default, and changing it means contacting a Visa Member Services representative.
Finix warns poor CEDP data can downgrade past transactions, and Stripe's CEDP reports carry data from two months earlier.

discover.text: Discover's US acquirer rates open only with an acquirer-issued code, and the Fed now requires controls that classify interchange for each acquirer and merchant.

opportunity.title: Class, rate and downgrade reason per transaction
opportunity.text: Show each transaction's card class, the programme it was priced and cleared at, and any downgrade reason. Cybersource already shows priced against cleared interchange with a reason code per transaction.
opportunity.stage_move: Show the class and rate each transaction was billed at

tasks.title: Review and pay the network invoice

does.text: The card team checks each network's bill against its processor's fee reports and pays it, usually by ACH. Mastercard bills weekly through MCBS, Visa invoices through its portal and Amex fees settle on the 26th.

touchpoints.name: Pricing and Billing Resource Center (Mastercard Connect)
Daily Activity Report Fee Detail Section

why.text: The UK regulator found issuers generally cope with scheme fee information, while US community banks describe long provider bills and retain billing consultants.

points.text: Reading a Visa invoice needs knowledge of settlement and collection entities, which Visa teaches as a course.
Every US issuer pays Visa Advanced Authorization fees whether or not it uses the data.
Mastercard reports are themselves billed, and Mastercard Academy sold a two-day MCBS billing seminar for USD 900.
ICBA told the Fed that most community banks struggled to get network and processing fee data from their technology providers. This is advocacy.

discover.text: PULSE sells Discover Debit on an all-in fee with a one-page invoice, and claims an issuer can reconcile it in about ten minutes.

opportunity.title: The one-page bill as the default view
opportunity.text: Carry the one-page invoice into the portal as the default view, one line per network with detail on demand. Community banks and credit unions complain of long bills that are hard to interpret.
opportunity.stage_move: Keep the short bill

tasks.title: Trace scheme fees to their triggers and pass them on

does.text: Acquirer analysts trace each scheme invoice line to the events behind it, allocate fees to merchants and model new fees. Payfacs and merchants see these costs only as their acquirer passes them on.

touchpoints.name: Torus and CardTraq network fee analytics
Stripe IC+ plan-level report for connected accounts

why.text: UK acquirers with over 90% of the market struggled with behavioural fees, and one firm's review team found several million pounds of incorrect scheme charges in a year.

points.text: Portal bulletin codes do not match invoice codes, and 13 Visa bulletins in 2024 omitted the billing event, so new fees surfaced first on the invoice.
Teya said a scheme billing line can hold several hundred events, each taking hours to trace.
UK acquirers could not identify which merchants triggered behavioural fees, so the cost spreads across all their merchants.
One acquirer had eight Mastercard fee trigger misalignments in two years, and another faced a multi-year clawback after Mastercard's own error.

discover.text: Payfacs and ISOs see Discover through acquirer pricing, often a blended rate, and merchants on flat plans cannot see migrated Discover debit rates.

opportunity.title: Every fee line traced to its trigger
opportunity.text: Give each invoice line a stable billing identifier, its trigger rule and a link to its transactions, free to download as data. Visa and Mastercard told the UK regulator they cannot supply this within a year.
opportunity.stage_move: Every fee line traces to its trigger

tasks.title: File quarterly and monthly programme reports

does.text: Issuers and programme managers compile portfolio returns for the networks, such as Mastercard's QMR due by the 15th. Amex GNS partners file monthly Program Progress Reports within 15 days, with an annual attestation.

touchpoints.name: Knowledge Base: Reporting Center, File Tracker, Program Progress Reports

why.text: The evidence shows fixed deadlines and fees, such as $250 a month for Amex portfolio reporting, and the study found no partner complaint about the work.

points.text: Amex GNS partners must file Program Progress Reports within 15 days of month end and attest to their accuracy each year.
Programmes on a processor rely on it to compile quarterly network reports, which Lithic delivers by the fifth business day after quarter end.

discover.text: Discover Debit is sold to community banks and credit unions with no quarterly reporting requirement, alongside its one-page invoice.

opportunity.title: Keep the no-reporting promise
opportunity.text: Discover Debit already spares small issuers quarterly reporting, so the study drew no separate design move for this task.

tasks.title: Take in a cardholder claim and start the clocks

does.text: Front-line staff take the cardholder's call, judge chargeback rights across network rules and pass the claim to a back-office specialist. Regulation E runs its own clock beside the network's.

touchpoints.name: Fiserv Dispute Expert and FIS CBK processor dispute products

why.text: ICBA's magazine says 74 per cent of consumers go straight to their bank and each dispute takes 2.5 calls.

points.text: Regulation E asks for a decision in 10 business days, or provisional credit and up to 45 days, on top of network limits.
Unit learns of disputes a day later from a daily file, after cardholders phone the processor.
A Jack Henry case study says members once had to visit a branch in set hours to fill in dispute forms.
ICBA says network dispute changes help merchants deny claims and leave banks with harder customer conversations.

discover.text: PULSE tells issuers to send cardholders to the merchant first, and Discover's issuer claim screens sit behind a sign-in.

opportunity.title: The legal clock beside the network clock
opportunity.text: Show Reg E provisional credit and decision deadlines next to chargeback deadlines on each case, from the cardholder contact date. The only public tool found that warns on the Reg E deadline is a processor portal.
opportunity.stage_move: Put the partner's own legal clock beside the network clock

tasks.title: Resolve the claim before it becomes a chargeback

does.text: Before a chargeback exists, the issuer's tool checks merchant data and resolution services, and enrolled merchants answer alerts or refund. Visa switched Rapid Dispute Resolution on for issuers by default.

why.text: Merchants pay per alert whatever the outcome, and Ethoca and CDRN overlap on Visa orders.

points.text: Merchants pay a fee for each alert whatever the outcome, and Ethoca and CDRN overlap on Visa orders.
A consultancy reports Mastercard's acquirer Collaboration route ends in the US and Canada on 4 January 2027 with no named replacement.
Mastercard Collaboration requests auto-reject after 72 hours, and merchants should acknowledge Ethoca alerts within 24 hours.
Acquirers had to stop counting or billing RDR credits as disputes once Visa flagged them.

discover.text: A practitioner guide finds no Discover equivalent of the main pre-dispute and compelling-evidence tools.

opportunity.title: Free pre-dispute resolution, counted as prevented
opportunity.text: Route each new claim through a merchant resolution step at no per-alert fee, and show resolved claims as prevented on partner reports. Visa already excludes pre-dispute resolutions from its monitoring ratio.
opportunity.stage_move: Offer free pre-dispute resolution and count it as prevented

tasks.title: Report confirmed fraud and act on compromise alerts

does.text: Fraud staff report each confirmed fraud to the network before disputing it, and turn compromised-card alert lists into block, monitor and reissue work.

why.text: Visa can suspend fraud dispute rights for 90 or 180 days after reporting failures, and credit unions reformat alert lists by hand several times a week.

points.text: Visa needs the fraud report within 60 days of the transaction before a fraud dispute can be raised.
Visa compromise alerts arrive only inside Visa Risk Manager, and loss recovery needs fraud reported within 120 days of the alert.
Mastercard's Fraud Notification Service caps fraud chargebacks at 35 per card account.
Discover fraud tool enrolment needs two named administrators, a Director or VP signature and an emailed form.

discover.text: Discover takes confirmed fraud through a separate portal enrolled by signed form, apart from its Disputes Portal.

opportunity.title: One action files the fraud report and the dispute
opportunity.text: Let one issuer action file the fraud report and open the dispute. Mastercom already lists the fraud report among claim actions, while Discover's portal offers only retrieval, chargeback and compliance tabs.
opportunity.stage_move: Fold fraud reporting into the dispute

tasks.title: Work the dispute queue to deadline

does.text: Analysts clear network work queues each day, accepting, answering or escalating each case inside its time limit. A missed deadline closes the cycle against the silent party.

why.text: Mastercard, which sells dispute tools, puts US issuer cost at about USD 9 to 10 per dispute, and one payfac analyst posting lists four network portals plus fax.

points.text: Vendors say that since April 2025 Visa acquirer fees rise with each day a dispute sits.
Discover status values such as Unable to Process describe the system result and say nothing about who acts next.
A processor or CUSO analyst needs a separate Discover user ID for each institution, and saved queues are visible only to their creator.
When VROL is down, a processor portal blocks every Visa action on the case until it reconnects.

discover.text: Discover's portal shows a Stage Expiration date, yet its status values name system results and never the next actor.

opportunity.title: Whose move it is and the days left
opportunity.text: Make each case status a next action with an owner and a day count from the condition's own limit, with the same states in the API. Amex and a PULSE processor wrapper already show this to their users.
opportunity.stage_move: Show whose move it is and the days left, on every case

tasks.title: Answer retrievals and submit evidence

does.text: Acquirers and merchants answer retrieval requests and chargebacks with documents inside each network's window. ATM acquirers answer non-receipt of cash claims with the disbursement record.

why.text: Compelling Evidence 3.0 gets one attempt and incomplete submissions are declined, while upload limits range from three images to 18 MB.

points.text: A processor gives merchants nine days to defend against the acquirer's 30.
Amex attachments can take up to seven days to load, with caps of 5MB per file and 25MB per case.
Discover conditional fields can turn mandatory as other fields are filled, and the error appears only on submit.
Mastercard codes ATM cases as free-text memos, while Visa names the journal fields an ATM acquirer returns.

discover.text: Discover's public merchant help lists Internet Explorer 6 and a three-image representment cap, though its issuer portal now takes 15 MB files.

opportunity.title: Evidence checked before it is final
opportunity.text: Check evidence against the reason code before submission, show limits up front and list items still missing inside the window. Mastercom's Pending Documentation Report shows the value of flagging gaps early.
opportunity.stage_move: Let evidence be checked before it is final

tasks.title: Escalate a case to pre-arbitration and arbitration

does.text: When a response fails, the issuer or acquirer files pre-arbitration and then arbitration, where Visa rules on prior exchanges only.

touchpoints.name: DN Disputes Portal Dispute Details page

why.text: Arbitration carries fees and short windows, such as USD 150 to file and USD 250 for review at Amex and a reported USD 600 for losing at Visa.

points.text: Visa arbitration must be filed within 10 days and is decided on prior exchanges, and an appeal needs new evidence and USD 5,000 at stake.
A Mastercard issuer has 15 days to escalate a rejected pre-arbitration, and an acquirer silent for 30 days is deemed to accept.
Discover's Dispute Rules Manual is not public, so time limits come from practitioners.
PULSE issuers cannot take card-not-present fraud to pre-arbitration, per Adyen.

discover.text: Discover and PULSE keep their dispute rules behind a login, while Mastercard publishes its Chargeback Guide and Visa its core rules.

opportunity.title: Public, dated dispute rules
opportunity.text: Publish the Discover and PULSE dispute rules and time limits with an effective date on each change, and one code list shared with the screens. Visa and Mastercard already publish theirs.
opportunity.stage_move: Make the dispute rules public and dated

tasks.title: Monitor fraud and chargeback ratios

does.text: Acquirers track each merchant's fraud and dispute ratio against network programmes every month, and payfacs meet those programmes through their acquirer. Issuers face their own Visa programme for excessive disputes or fraud.

touchpoints.name: Data Integrity application on Mastercard Connect
MATCH Pro and FLD scam listings

why.text: Merchants cannot see the items behind their VAMP ratio, and the FTC's 2026 orders against Nuvei and Humboldt centre on chargeback screening failures.

points.text: Stripe tells merchants VAMP data is reported a month late and shows its own daily estimates alongside.
VAMP fee amounts are absent from the public rulebook, and a European acquirer's guidance contradicted Visa's fact sheet on RDR exclusion.
Issuers in Visa's VIMP face assessments rising to USD 100,000 a month.
Practitioners report Mastercard moves chargeback and fraud monitoring to the sub-merchant ID from April 2027.

discover.text: The study found no public Discover monitoring line, and vendors cite about 1 per cent and 100 chargebacks a month.

opportunity.title: A published line with every counted item
opportunity.text: Publish Discover's dispute and fraud thresholds, and give acquirers a live ratio per merchant and sub-merchant with every counted item listed.
opportunity.stage_move: Publish the monitoring line and show the items behind the ratio

tasks.title: Triage the week's network bulletins

does.text: A named contact reads each network's bulletins, judges which apply and passes them on inside the firm or to clients. Visa emails weekly Business News, Mastercard posts announcements and Amex publishes monthly updates.

why.text: The primary bulletins are private, so most partners meet change second hand through processors and forwarded mail.

points.text: A Visa Notification takes effect when sent, and Business News reaches only two named roles who must distribute it.
A mandate can reach a credit union through its EFT processor, its core CUSO and its own inbox.
Fiserv's merchant notice opens with a general warning and does not state which merchants are affected.
Large acquirers staff people to turn scheme mandates and bulletins into system requirements.

discover.text: No Discover or PULSE bulletin is public, so their format and lead times cannot be judged.

opportunity.title: A change ledger with a verdict for each partner
opportunity.text: Publish each change as one ledger item typed action, legal or information, and tell each partner whether it acts, its processor has handled it, or nothing is needed. Processors write that verdict today.
opportunity.stage_move: Change ledger with a verdict per partner

tasks.title: Implement a twice-yearly release or mandate

does.text: Processors certify each April and October release and tell clients what changed, while acquirers turn mandates into requirements for their own systems.

why.text: Acquirers and payfacs describe compressed timelines, and a core CUSO says mandates arrive with required programming changes and short deadlines.

points.text: Smaller institutions struggle to absorb core provider charges for updates, and one community bank's tokenisation stalled while it waited on its core.
A payfac filing says networks can change rules with or without advance notice.
Stripe staffs a Card Network Office role to review twice-yearly releases for business impact.
Mastercard's change cadence differs by product.

discover.text: Processors say recent Discover and PULSE releases asked nothing of their clients, and Marqeta records no applicable changes for October 2026.

opportunity.title: A quiet cycle, said by the network
opportunity.text: When a release asks nothing of a partner, the network says so by name and date. Today only processors voice Discover's light change burden.
opportunity.stage_move: A quiet cycle, said plainly

tasks.title: Request a waiver or extension

does.text: A partner that cannot meet a mandate on time asks for a waiver, variance or extension. Visa routes it through a representative, Mastercard through Variance Manager and Amex through a published extension route.

touchpoints.name: Visa waiver request through the Visa representative
Business and Operational Policies extension route

why.text: Visa waivers carry an assessment and set no precedent, and large payment firms staff roles to manage waiver requests.

points.text: Each Visa waiver is unique and answered in writing, so each bank relitigates similar requests.
Mastercard noncompliance assessments can be appealed within 30 days for a fee of up to USD 500.
Amex policy changes take effect on publication, and a participant must document the impact to ask for up to three months.

discover.text: Discover's account executive owns contracts and configuration changes, and the study found no public Discover extension route.

opportunity.title: Request more time from inside the change
opportunity.text: Attach a request-more-time action to each change, with the decision rule stated and a tracked status. Amex already publishes a three-month route it says it will not unreasonably withhold.
opportunity.stage_move: Extension request inside the change

tasks.title: Raise a support case and chase the answer

does.text: Staff raise problems by phone, case tool, mailbox or account executive, depending on the network and urgency. Mastercard sends urgent issues to Customer Technical Services by phone and others to Support Case Management.

touchpoints.name: Discover Operations Center and Network Command Center

why.text: UK acquirers holding over 65 percent of the market had difficulty getting timely and adequate answers from the schemes.

points.text: Discover client services are spread across function-specific mailboxes, and its operations desk keeps Eastern business hours and closes on twelve holidays.
PULSE publishes Central-time business hours only, with a two-business-day callback as its one response commitment.
The public Amex GNS contact route is a web form that issues a case number, with no phone or hours.
Visa's developer terms say Visa has no obligation to provide support.

discover.text: Discover splits a 24x7 Network Command Center from a business-hours Operations Center, and PULSE publishes no 24x7 line, where Mastercard and Visa describe round-the-clock client support.

opportunity.title: One support map with hours and response times
opportunity.text: Publish one support map by partner type and problem, each route with hours and a response commitment, including a round-the-clock path for small institutions. SHAZAM already staffs client service 24/7/365.
opportunity.stage_move: One support map with hours and clocks

tasks.title: Live through a network incident

does.text: During an outage the partner detects the problem, phones the network help desk and relays updates to its own customers. Partners must also report their own outages and data compromises to the network.

why.text: An independent review found Visa's 2018 outage communications were not timely, regular or actionable, and the UK regulator now requires yearly testing with participants.

points.text: No public status page for core authorisation and settlement was found for any of the four networks.
Amex leaves detection of a network outage to the acquirer, which is told to phone the help desk.
Mastercard shares its Post Incident Report through the customer's account manager.
The National ATM Council's jackpotting guidance lists police and federal agencies and names no card network contact.

discover.text: Discover runs a 24x7 Network Command Center with a second-escalation manager, and like its peers publishes no core network status page.

opportunity.title: A partner status view for the core network
opportunity.text: Run a partner status view for authorisation, settlement, portals and APIs, with subscriptions, a declared update rhythm and a post-incident report every partner can read. Networks publish status today only for APIs and gateway products.
opportunity.stage_move: Partner status for the core network

tasks.title: Attest compliance and answer network questionnaires

does.text: Partners sign yearly attestations and answer periodic network questionnaires. Amex wants an annual attestation for Program Progress Reports, and Discover a yearly PCI attestation from payment enablers.

why.text: Violations draw escalating fees, up to USD 20,000 for repeat intermediary violations at Amex, and a processor passes network fines through to ATM ISOs.

points.text: Amex violations follow a determination, notification and Action Plan process with escalating fees.
Amex's October 2025 rules added portfolio accountability and fees of up to USD 20,000 for repeat intermediary violations.
CDS relayed Visa's October 2025 operator rules with warnings of suspension and fines, and passes network fines through to the ISO.
Discover compliance filing runs through a shared mailbox with no status view. That is the study's inference.

discover.text: Discover asks payment enablers for a yearly PCI attestation by email, and offers chip merchants with a tested incident plan relief through SCIP.

opportunity.title: No separate move drawn
opportunity.text: The study drew no design move for attestation itself. Its operational review move lists attestations due as one input.

tasks.title: Prepare and hold the business review

does.text: The partner reviews portfolio performance, operations and plans with its named relationship owner, and Mastercard key accounts also get a quarterly operational review. Network tools such as the PULSE Debit Dashboard and Visa Analytics Platform supply peer comparisons.

why.text: A PULSE account executive says most issuers do not know their own interchange or costs, and UK acquirers buy scheme services to understand their own fees.

points.text: Most issuers do not know the exact interchange they earn or their total costs, according to a PULSE account executive.
UK acquirers told the regulator they buy extra scheme services to understand their own fees.
Visa and Mastercard sell consulting and advisory work as paid lines.
Mastercard runs quarterly operational reviews for key accounts only, so the study infers that smaller issuers may never get one.

discover.text: The PULSE Debit Dashboard is open to every PULSE issuer, with revenue, expense and approvals by BIN, interchange by category and a peer comparison.

opportunity.title: Business review built on shared data
opportunity.text: The Debit Dashboard model would extend across the family, and the business and operational review would be generated from what the partner already sees. Partners without an account manager would get it too.
opportunity.stage_move: Business review built on shared data

tasks.title: Track incentive commitments and payments

does.text: A partner on an incentive contract works to volume, issuance or conversion commitments and receives payments the network calculates. The network checks with the client whether obligations were met.

touchpoints.name: Mastercard Pricing and Billing Resource Center

why.text: No partner-facing incentive tracker was found at any network and earned incentives are estimated from forecasts, while the clawback evidence rests on DOJ allegations against Visa.

points.text: Visa and Mastercard estimate earned incentives from forecasts, and Visa uses client-reported data as one input.
Mastercard checks drafted contracts for term, clawbacks and customer commitments.
DOJ alleges a debit issuer missing Visa's growth requirement could owe earned benefits back plus a fixed fee.
DOJ alleges nearly 1,000 Visa issuing contracts carry volume incentives that deter adding debit networks.

discover.text: Discover runs fixed-term incentive deals without publishing amounts, and no partner-facing tracker was seen at any network.

opportunity.title: Incentive ledger in the partner record
opportunity.text: Each commitment would show its measure, the partner's standing, who supplied the data and payment status, including any clawback trigger. Visa and Mastercard track these in internal files, billing systems and quarterly reviews.
opportunity.stage_move: Incentive ledger in the partner record

tasks.title: Add a service or product

does.text: The partner asks for a new network service, tool or API and waits for enrolment, approval or a contract change. Self-service ordering exists only in patches, such as the Mastercard Connect Store and Amex Service Enrollment.

why.text: Discover enrols by PDF, web form or account executive, and a new Visa API means a new commercial step.

points.text: Discover enrols fraud products through application PDFs and web forms.
New DebitProtect clients enrol through a PULSE account executive with no self-service route.
Adding a Discover API depends on a representative and an agreement change.
Adding a Visa API sets production pricing per use case in a VDP API Agreement.

discover.text: Discover enrols by PDF, form or account executive, while the Mastercard Connect Store offers Request, checkout scoped by BIN and Track Orders.

opportunity.title: One catalogue with Request and order tracking
opportunity.text: Every service would carry an Included or Priced marker and a Request action scoped to BINs, with approver sign-off and a tracked order. The Mastercard Connect Store sets this pattern.
opportunity.stage_move: One catalogue with Request and order tracking

tasks.title: Expand into a new market or role

does.text: An acquirer applies to extend its licence into a new country, a payfac moves large merchants to direct agreements, and a sponsor seeks approval for each new programme manager.

why.text: Growth rules exist at Mastercard, Visa and Amex, and each adds an application, certification or approval.

points.text: A Visa payfac must move any sponsored merchant above 1 million dollars a year onto a direct acquirer agreement.
A consultancy says crossing the OptBlue threshold means signing a direct agreement with its own review.
Since May 2025 a BIN sponsor needs Mastercard's approval per programme manager, revocable without notice.
The study found no public Discover procedure for expanding into a market.

discover.text: Discover's growth runs case by case through an account executive and the EASI Message Center, with no public expansion path.

opportunity.title: Growth paths inside the record
opportunity.text: The partner record would show the next step, such as a new country, role or threshold, with eligibility and what changes. Mastercard and Amex already publish growth steps and thresholds.
opportunity.stage_move: Growth paths inside the record

tasks.title: Negotiate the renewal

does.text: Before a fixed term ends, the network seeks renewal and the partner renegotiates incentives and commitments with its relationship owner. Some banks hire consultants to bargain.

touchpoints.name: Visa account team and Client Success manager

why.text: Terms are negotiated privately, and a consultancy cites a client that more than doubled its incentives at renewal.

points.text: A bank consultancy says networks negotiate incentive offers with banks and credit unions in give-and-take fashion.
Engage fi cites a client that got more than twice its previous card brand incentives at renewal.
DOJ alleges over 180 large merchants and acquirers hold de facto exclusive Visa deals.
From April 2026 Mastercard added services to a US bundle fee and raised its rate, per a merchant advisory.

discover.text: Discover's deferred incentive balance was 28 million dollars at end-2024 against billions at Visa and Mastercard, and its owner says rivals pay large signing bonuses.

opportunity.title: Renewal workspace over the whole term
opportunity.text: Renewal would open early with term economics, services used, commitments met and an incumbent-incentive line the partner fills in. Networks renew in advance, and regulators are forcing fee clarity.
opportunity.stage_move: Renewal workspace over the whole term

tasks.title: Exit the network or sell the portfolio

does.text: A leaving partner gives notice, cancels cards or helps merchants move, and releases its identifiers. A partner selling a portfolio notifies the network first.

why.text: Exit rules impose long waits and lasting liability, and the early termination fees and clawbacks rest on DOJ allegations against Visa.

points.text: A Visa member cannot finish leaving until every BIN is released, and each must sit inactive for 120 days first.
Maestro and Cirrus principals give a year's notice, cancel all cards and get no refund of fees.
When a Mastercard principal leaves, each sponsored affiliate must wind down unless another principal sponsors it in time.
i3 Verticals says losing its sponsor without migrating its payfac portfolio would stop its business.

discover.text: Discover publishes no exit terms, and its owner competes with partner issuers.

opportunity.title: Written exit terms with a leaving checklist
opportunity.text: Discover would publish what leaving requires and what survives, including BIN release, cardholder and merchant notices, data export and transfer help. Mastercard and Visa already publish exit rules.
opportunity.stage_move: Written exit terms with a leaving checklist
